claims.text: The starting material is additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 with a fine-grained FCC matrix.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed largely by the composition, continuity, stability, and adhesion of the surface oxide scale.
Grain boundaries provide diffusion paths for ionic or cationic species during oxidation.
A fine-grained microstructure with a higher grain-boundary density accelerates ionic diffusion relative to a coarse-grained microstructure.
The accelerated grain-boundary transport particularly involves Cr and Ti cations.
Outward diffusion of Cr along grain boundaries can produce surface chromia.
Dense and continuous Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scales can protect an alloy by limiting oxygen ingress and outward cation transport.
Rapid grain-boundary transport in the fine-grained starting state undermines protective chromia or alumina formation and instead promotes non-protective mixed oxides or spinels.
The spinel phases interrupting the protective scale are brittle and porous.
Thermal stress or prolonged exposure causes the compromised oxide scale to crack and spall.
Scale spallation permits oxygen ingress, accelerates bulk degradation, and can ultimately cause catastrophic failure.
Post-deposition annealing can significantly coarsen the grains and reduce grain-boundary density without changing the alloy's overall composition.
The annealed coarse-grained sample will develop a thinner, more uniform, and more adherent protective oxide scale than the fine-grained baseline.
The annealed sample will exhibit less scale spallation and better elevated-temperature stability than the fine-grained baseline.
The fine-grained baseline will form a thicker, more porous oxide with more spinel, cracking, and spallation.
The proposed behavior applies at temperatures of approximately 900 °C and above in both oxidizing and CO/H2-containing reducing atmospheres.
Within the stated exposure boundaries, oxide-scale evolution is kinetically dominated by grain-boundary diffusion.
The specific contribution of Ti to oxide morphology and failure dynamics is uncertain.

Failure of grain coarsening to produce a statistically significant improvement in scale continuity, non-protective-phase thickness, or spallation resistance would falsify the proposed grain-boundary mechanism.
